decisions.reason: As a recent launch that extends the firm's core secure communication and second-channel authentication offer, it is strategically central and management is likely to continue backing it.
This mobile digital-signature function fits the firm's stated move toward app-based interactions and online signing, so recent investment and public commitment make withdrawal unlikely.
A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture sits very close to the firm's technical core and likely absorbed substantial R&D effort, which strongly favors continued commitment.
Although somewhat more specialized, it still builds on the firm's secure messaging direction and management can readily justify weaker early traction as temporary market adoption effects.

The hardware signature token is somewhat less central to the firm's broader software-led ecosystem direction, but it remains close enough to the core offer that management would probably retain it for now.

The compliance suite leverages the firm's security and regulatory positioning, and given the industry's growth and the product's recent launch, management is likely to persist rather than exit quickly.
